skill.name: env-and-assets-bootstrap
skill.description: Prepare conservative conda-first environment plans and asset assumptions for README-documented AI reproduction repositories before running experiments.
skill.summary: Plan reproducible environment setup and asset paths before AI repository runs.
skill.author: lllllllama

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are markdown formatting or conservative policy text and are false positives. The Python bootstrapper does execute package manager commands, so users should treat non-dry-run installs on untrusted repositories as risky.

remediation.issue: The bootstrapper can execute package installation commands for a target repository.
remediation.suggestion: Make dry-run the default or require explicit confirmation before subprocess.run executes installers. Warn users that pip and conda installs can run build hooks.

content.value_statement: Research repositories often need careful environment and asset setup before runs. This skill creates conservative conda-first plans, cache assumptions, and setup notes.
actual_capabilities: Detects common top-level environment files and proposes conservative setup steps.
Prefers conda or mamba when available, with virtualenv as a fallback.
Generates platform-specific activation guidance for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Builds asset manifests for datasets, checkpoints, weights, cache, and output paths.
Scans README and config files for documented asset URLs and path hints.
Records unresolved setup risks instead of guessing missing dependency details.
limitations: Works best after a reproduction target and README setup path are already selected.
Does not choose papers, select repositories, or judge final experiment results.
Does not verify that external checkpoints or datasets are authentic.
Non-dry-run bootstrapping may install packages from the target repository.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Research Repo Run
use_cases.description: Create a cautious environment plan before installing dependencies or launching experiments.

use_cases.title: Document Asset Requirements
use_cases.description: List expected checkpoints, datasets, caches, and local paths before reproduction work begins.

use_cases.title: Standardize Setup Reviews
use_cases.description: Produce repeatable setup notes for teams reviewing many AI research repositories.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Basic Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup planning for one repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a conservative environment setup plan for this README-documented reproduction repository. Include detected environment files, activation steps, and unresolved risks.

prompt_templates.title: Map Assets Before Running
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the README and config hints for datasets, checkpoints, weights, and cache paths. Produce an asset plan with sources and missing items.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Setup Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a conda-first setup plan, then describe the virtualenv fallback. Note platform differences and dependency uncertainties.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Full Bootstrap Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this repository setup for install risks before any non-dry-run bootstrap. Identify commands, asset assumptions, and confirmation points.

output_examples.input: A repository has an environment.yml file and README checkpoint links.
output: Environment file detected and conda setup recommended.
Activation guidance includes the declared environment name.
Checkpoint links are listed with target local paths and unresolved authenticity notes.

output_examples.input: A repository has requirements.txt but no documented datasets.
output: Virtualenv setup is proposed with a requirements installation step.
Dataset and cache groups are marked missing or unknown.
The report asks for primary source confirmation before downloading assets.

output_examples.input: A team wants to review setup safety before running installers.
output: The plan separates dry-run review from package installation.
Installer commands are identified for explicit user confirmation.
Untrusted repository risks are documented before execution.

best_practices: Run planning and dry-run steps before installing packages from a new repository.
Prefer documented README and environment files over inferred dependency choices.
Record asset sources, local paths, and unresolved authenticity risks clearly.
anti_patterns: Do not treat inferred asset URLs as canonical without primary source support.
Do not run non-dry-run bootstraps on untrusted repositories without review.
Do not use this skill as a replacement for final reproduction result analysis.

faq.question: Does this skill run experiments?
faq.answer: No. It prepares environment and asset assumptions before any experiment run.

faq.question: Which environment manager does it prefer?
faq.answer: It prefers conda or mamba when available, then falls back to virtualenv.

faq.question: Can it find checkpoint and dataset hints?
faq.answer: Yes. It scans README and config files for documented URLs, paths, and asset keywords.

faq.question: Does it verify downloaded assets?
faq.answer: No. It records source hints and unresolved risks, but users must verify authenticity.

faq.question: Is non-dry-run bootstrapping safe for unknown repositories?
faq.answer: It should be reviewed first because package installers can execute project build logic.

faq.question: Can teams use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
